newsitem.title: USA: U.S. domestic spending up 2.2 pct in 1996 - Census.
newsitem.headline: U.S. domestic spending up 2.2 pct in 1996 - Census.

text.p: U.S. government domestic spending as measured by the Commerce Department's Census Bureau rose 2.2 percent in 1996 to $1.4 trillion, the department said on Wednesday.

The figure includes grants, benefits, subsidies and salaries, as well as goods and services purchased. But it excludes interest on federal debt and other federal payments that could not be allocated geographically.
In a pair of reports, the Census Bureau attributed the increase to a rise in direct payments to individuals.
The reports said federal government payroll expenditures totaled $170 billion in 1996, up one percent from 1995. Federal procurement contract obligations fell one percent in 1996 to $201 billion.
Regionally, California received more federal funds than any other state, followed by New York and Texas. Virginia topped the list in federal funding per capita, followed by Maryland and Alaska.
